enc.title: Blackbody lab: what if $h$ shrinks?
enc.intro:
The Planck function $B_
u= rac{2h
u^3}{c^2} rac{1}{e^{h
u/k_BT}-1}$ has two limits: Rayleigh–Jeans for $h
u\ll k_BT$ and Wien for $h
u\gg k_BT$. Move $T$ and watch the peak; then scale $h$ down to see what the world would look like without quantisation.
tasks: Set $T=2.725$ K (the CMB): at which frequency does $B_\nu$ peak? Compare with the exam values (about 160 GHz, $\lambda_{\max}\approx1$ mm).
Predict first: if you double $T$, how do the peak frequency and the peak height change? Then check ($\nu_{\max}\propto T$, $B_{\max}\propto T^3$).
Switch on the CMB curve next to the Sun ($T=5800$ K): by how many orders of magnitude do they differ at $10^{11}$ Hz, and why is the Rayleigh–Jeans line a good description of the CMB there?
Slide $h$ down towards 0: the peak runs away to higher frequency. What does the curve become, and why does $\int B_\nu\,d\nu$ then diverge (ultraviolet catastrophe)?

enc.title: Rotation curves: remove the black hole, remove the halo
enc.intro: A galaxy with a central black hole $M_0$ and a dark-matter halo with $\rho\propto r^{-2}$ has enclosed mass $M_r=kr+M_0$, hence $v_c=\sqrt{G(k+M_0/r)}$ (Winter 2024, Q4). Switch each ingredient on and off and see which one controls which radius.
tasks: Switch the halo off: what does $v_c(r)$ look like? (Keplerian, $v\propto r^{-1/2}$). Then switch it on and the black hole off: what is $v_c$ at large and small $r$?
Predict: for $M_0=4\times10^6\,M_\odot$ and $v=110$ km/s at 2 pc, how big must $k$ be? Compare with the value shown ($8.1\times10^5\,M_\odot$/pc).
At what radius does the halo start to dominate the black hole? (Set $M_0/r=k$.)
A flat rotation curve means $M_r\propto r$. Why does that imply $\rho\propto r^{-2}$?

source.where: Open question 4 (galaxy with black hole and r^-2 halo)
Open question 6 (flat rotation curve, escape velocity)

enc.title: Friedmann lab: what if $\Lambda$ or matter disappears?
enc.intro: With $H_0=1$ the Friedmann equation reads $\dot a^2=\Omega_m/a+\Omega_r/a^2+\Omega_k+\Omega_\Lambda a^2$ with $\Omega_k=1-\Omega_m-\Omega_\Lambda$. Change the content of the universe and watch $a(t)$, its age and its fate.
tasks: Set $\Omega_m=1$, $\Omega_\Lambda=0$ (Einstein–de Sitter): the age should be $\frac23H_0^{-1}$ and $a\propto t^{2/3}$. Check it.
Predict: does adding $\Omega_\Lambda=0.7$ make the universe older or younger than $\frac23H_0^{-1}$? Check the age (0.96 $H_0^{-1}$).

Raise $\Omega_m$ to 2 with no $\Lambda$: the universe is closed. Find the time of maximum expansion and the big crunch. Compare with the exam result $t=\pi\Omega_m/(\Omega_m-1)^{3/2}\,H_0^{-1}$ ($=2\pi$ here).
Remove the matter completely and keep only $\Lambda$: what does $a(t)$ do (exponential growth)?

source.where: Open question 7 (Friedmann with equation of state w)

enc.title: Diatomic chain: acoustic and optical branches
enc.intro: A chain with two atoms per cell (masses $M_1$, $M_2$, spring $k$) has $\omega^2=k\left(\frac1{M_1}+\frac1{M_2}\right)\pm k\sqrt{\left(\frac1{M_1}+\frac1{M_2}\right)^2-\frac{2}{M_1M_2}(1-\cos qa)}$. Change the mass ratio, move along the dispersion and watch how the atoms move.
tasks: Slide $qa/\pi$ towards 1 on the acoustic branch: what happens to the group velocity $d\omega/dq$ at the zone edge? Why (standing wave)?
Predict: at $q=0$, how do the two atoms move on the optical branch? ($V/U=-M_1/M_2$: opposite directions, the centre of mass at rest). Check the animation.
Increase $M_2/M_1$: how do the two edge frequencies $\sqrt{2k/M_{heavy}}$ and $\sqrt{2k/M_{light}}$ and the gap between them change?
Press 'make the masses equal': what happens to the gap, and what is the chain now?

enc.title: Debye versus Einstein: why $T^3$?
enc.intro: The Debye model uses the linear dispersion $\omega=v_sq$ up to a cut-off $\omega_D$ ($C_V\propto T^3$ at low $T$, Dulong–Petit at high $T$); the Einstein model uses one single frequency.
tasks: Predict first: at $T=\Theta_D/10$ which model gives the larger heat capacity? Check, and read the $T^3$ law value.
Which model freezes out exponentially at low $T$, and why can a single frequency not produce a power law?
What is $C_V/3Nk_B$ at $T=\Theta_D$? Is Dulong–Petit already reached there?
Change $\Theta_D$ (stiffer or softer solid): which curve moves and how does the Debye $T^3$ coefficient depend on $\Theta_D$?

enc.title: The Fermi sea: switch the Pauli principle off
enc.intro: Electrons fill states from the bottom up: occupation $f=1/(e^{(E-\mu)/k_BT}+1)$ times the density of states $\nu\propto\sqrt E$. Compare with a classical gas without exclusion principle at the same density and temperature.
tasks: Copper has $n=8.5\times10^{28}$ m$^{-3}$. Predict $E_F$ (about 7 eV) and $T_F$, then check. How does $E_F$ scale with $n$?
At 300 K, what fraction of the electrons can be thermally excited? ($\sim T/T_F$). How wide is the smeared edge of the occupation compared with $E_F$?
Switch the Pauli principle off: what is the mean energy per electron now ($\frac32k_BT$) compared with $\frac35E_F$, and what would the heat capacity be?
Increase $T$ until $k_BT\sim E_F$: what happens to the shape (degenerate to classical)?

source.where: Problem 2a (free-electron metals: Fermi surface, DOS, specific heat)

enc.title: 2D crystal, reciprocal lattice and neutron peaks
enc.intro: This is Problem 1 of the Zheludev exam (Jan 2024, the default settings $a=6$ Å, $b=4$ Å, $\lambda=2.36$ Å): a 2D lattice with a two-atom basis at $(0,0)$ and $(\frac12,\frac12)$. Here $f_1$ is the corner atom and $f_2$ the centre atom (in the exam the labels are the other way round, which does not change $|f_1-f_2|/(f_1+f_2)$). The table lists the full scattering angle $\varphi=2\theta$ between $\vec k_i$ and $\vec k_f$; the exam key quotes the Bragg angle $\theta=\varphi/2$. The August 2024 variant (a $4\times5$ Å cell with basis $(0,0),(\frac13,\frac13)$) is not a slider setting; use $a=4$, $b=5$ to check the angles ($\theta=39.5^\circ$ and $22.2^\circ$) and compute its structure factor $F=f(1+e^{2\pi i(h+k)/3})$ by hand. The right panel shows the reciprocal lattice, the dot size is the intensity $|F|^2$, and the table lists the Bragg angles for the chosen wavelength.
tasks: Set $a=6$ Å, $b=4$ Å, $\gamma=90^\circ$, $f_2=f_1$: which reflections vanish and why? (The structure factor $F=f_1+f_2e^{i\pi(h+k)}$ cancels for $h+k$ odd: the cell is secretly centred.)
Predict the area of the first Brillouin zone before reading it off: $(2\pi)^2/A$.

Set $f_2=2f_1$ (exam: $f_1=2f_2$ with the labels swapped): compute $I(2,1)/I(1,1)$ by hand ($=1/9$) and compare with the dot sizes. Read off the angles for $(2,1)$ and $(1,1)$ at $\lambda=2.36$ Å: $\theta=29.5^\circ$ and $20.8^\circ$ (key: 29.47 and 20.73).
Make the lattice oblique ($\gamma=120^\circ$, $a=b$): what shape do the Wigner–Seitz cell and the Brillouin zone take? Change $\lambda$: which peaks disappear when $|G|>2k$?

enc.title: Oscillator states: when does $\langle x\rangle$ move?
enc.intro: Superpose oscillator eigenstates $\psi_n$ and watch $|\psi(x,t)|^2$ ($\hbar=m=\omega=1$). Then switch to a coherent state $|\alpha\rangle$, the eigenstate of the lowering operator.
tasks: Choose $n_1=0$, $n_2=1$ with weight 0.5: $\langle x\rangle$ oscillates. Predict what happens for $n_1=0$, $n_2=2$, then check (the matrix element $\langle0|x|2\rangle=0$).
Pick two states with odd difference but not neighbours (e.g. $n_1=0$, $n_2=3$): does $\langle x\rangle$ move? ($\langle n|x|m\rangle\ne0$ only for $m=n\pm1$: it does not.)
Switch to the coherent state: how does $\langle x\rangle(t)$ compare with the classical oscillator, and does the packet spread? ($\Delta x\,\Delta p=\hbar/2$ for all times.)
Set weight 0 or 1 (a single eigenstate): why is $|\psi|^2$ independent of time?

enc.title: Perturbation theory: where it works and where it fails
enc.intro: Two levels $\mp\Delta/2$ coupled by $V$: exact $E_\pm=\pm\frac12\sqrt{\Delta^2+4V^2}$. Compare with non-degenerate second-order perturbation theory $E_1\approx\varepsilon_1-V^2/\Delta$.
tasks: Predict where second-order theory fails and check on the plot (near $\Delta\approx2V$, where the denominator $\varepsilon_1-\varepsilon_2$ is small).
At $\Delta=0$ the levels are degenerate: what are the exact energies and what does degenerate first-order theory give? ($\pm V$)
Switch the coupling off: what is left? Switch it on and increase $V$: how does the minimal gap grow? (avoided crossing, $2V$)
Connect: the $\lambda(a^2+a^{\dagger2})$ perturbation of the oscillator couples $|n\rangle$ and $|n+2\rangle$: which levels repel each other?

enc.title: Uniform star: where does the burning happen?
enc.intro: A star of constant density in hydrostatic equilibrium has $P(r)=\frac{2\pi}{3}G\rho^2(R^2-r^2)$. With the ideal gas law $T(r)=\mu m_HP/(\rho k_B)\propto R^2-r^2$, and an energy generation rate $\varepsilon\propto T^n$ the burning is concentrated near the centre. Change $n$, switch to radiation pressure, or remove the $T$ dependence.
tasks: Set $n=4$ and look for $\varepsilon=0.1\,\varepsilon_c$: predict $r/R=\sqrt{1-0.1^{1/4}}$ first, then check the yellow marker (about 0.66).
Predict: does the burning region get larger or smaller for $n=16$ (CNO) than for $n=4$ (pp)? Check at the same fraction 0.1.
Switch to radiation pressure: $T\propto(R^2-r^2)^{1/4}$. Predict the new radius for $n=4$ ($r/R=\sqrt{1-0.1}=0.95$) and explain why the core is so much broader.
Double $\rho$ at fixed mass: how do $R$, $P_c$ and $T_c$ scale (use $R\propto\rho^{-1/3}$, $P_c\propto\rho^{4/3}$, $T_c\propto\rho^{1/3}$)?

source.where: Open question 1 (uniform-density star, hydrostatic equilibrium, eps ~ T^4): radius where eps = 0.1 eps_c
hydrostatic equilibrium and virial theorem notes

enc.title: Eddington limit versus the mass-luminosity relation
enc.intro: The Eddington luminosity $L_{Edd}=4\pi cGM/\chi$ is linear in $M$, the main-sequence luminosity grows like $M^3$ or $M^{3.5}$. They cross at the maximum stable stellar mass. Change the opacity or remove electron scattering and see what happens to the crossing point.
tasks: Predict from $M^3=3.3\times10^4\,M$ (in solar units) the crossing mass (about $180\,M_\odot$), then check the yellow dot.
Change $\alpha$ from 3 to 3.5: predict the new crossing mass from $M^{\alpha-1}=3.3\times10^4$ (about 64) before moving the slider.
Halve the opacity: by what factor do $L_{Edd}$ and the crossing mass change for $\alpha=3$ (factor 2 and $\sqrt2$)?
Switch off electron scattering: what happens to the limit, and what does that mean for radiation-driven winds from hot stars?

source.where: Eddington luminosity / maximum stellar mass (see the stellar-forge room for the exact problem)

enc.title: Resistivity: Matthiessen, defects and the Hall coefficient
enc.intro: In the Drude picture $\rho=m/(ne^2\tau)$. Scattering rates from defects and phonons add (Matthiessen), $\rho(T)=\rho_0+\rho_{ph}(T)$, with $\rho_{ph}\propto T^5$ below and $\propto T$ above the Debye temperature. The Hall coefficient $R_H=-1/(ne)$ does not care about scattering at all.
tasks: Predict $\rho(T\to0)$ before switching the phonons off: what remains, and what does the residual resistivity measure?
Remove the defects: how does $\rho(300\,\mathrm{K})$ change for a good (3 nΩ·m) versus a dirty (100 nΩ·m) sample? Which part of the curve moves?
Change $n$ with all else fixed: predict how $R_H$, $\tau$ and the Hall mobility $|R_H|/\rho$ react.
Double $\Theta_D$ and read the slope of $\rho(T)$ at high $T$; why is it $\propto1/\Theta_D$?

source.where: chapters on Drude model, Hall effect and electron-phonon scattering

enc.title: 1D cosine bands: effective mass and carrier densities
enc.intro: A 1D crystal with tight-binding bands $E_c=E_G-2t_c(\cos ka-1)$ and $E_v=2t_v(\cos ka-1)$ has effective masses $m^*=\hbar^2/(2ta^2)$. The electron and hole densities follow from integrating the Fermi function over the Brillouin zone; the chemical potential adjusts so that $n=p$ in the intrinsic case.
tasks: Predict $m_c^*$ and $m_v^*$ for $t_c=1$ eV, $t_v=2$ eV, $a=0.5$ nm before reading the panel.
Where does the intrinsic $\mu$ sit at $T\to0$ and where at high $T$ when $m_v\ne m_c$? Predict the sign of the shift $\frac{k_BT}{4}\ln(m_v^*/m_c^*)$, then raise $T$.
Switch on equal curvature: where is $\mu$ now and why is it exactly mid-gap?
Move $\mu$ by hand towards the conduction band: predict how $n$ and $p$ change, and which product stays fixed (mass action) while $\mu$ is in the gap.

source.where: Problem 3 (effective masses, carrier densities, chemical potential)

enc.title: Curie-Weiss: what does the exchange do to 1/chi?
enc.intro: Above the ordering temperature, $\chi=C/(T-T_W)$ and $1/\chi$ is a straight line that crosses the $T$ axis at the Weiss temperature $T_W$. In mean-field theory $T_W$ is set by the exchange: positive for ferromagnets, negative for antiferromagnets. Without exchange you get the pure Curie law.
tasks: Predict $T_W$ for $S=1/2$, $J_1=1$ meV, $z_1=6$ ($T_W=\frac{2S(S+1)}{3k_B}z_1J_1\approx35$ K) before reading it off.
Switch the exchange off: predict where the line crosses the axis, and how the slope $1/C$ depends on $S$.
Make $J_1$ negative: where does the line cross now, and why is the real transition (Néel) still at positive $T$?
Choose $J_1>0$ and $J_2<0$ such that $T_W=0$: what does the 1/χ line look like, and does it mean there is no magnetism?

source.where: MC (r) sign of the exchange energy J
Ch. 6.1-6.3 (pp. 136–161): Pauli, Landau, Hubbard/Stoner, exchange, mean field, Curie-Weiss, ferro- and antiferromagnets

enc.title: Spin 1/2 in a magnetic field: Larmor precession
enc.intro: For $H=-\gamma\vec B\cdot\vec S$ the expectation value obeys $d\langle\vec S\rangle/dt=\gamma\langle\vec S\rangle\times\vec B$: the Bloch vector precesses about $\vec B$ at the Larmor frequency $\omega=\gamma B$. Start in different directions, tilt the field, or switch it off.
tasks: Start along $+x$ with $\vec B\parallel\hat z$: predict $\langle S_x\rangle(t)$, $\langle S_y\rangle(t)$, $\langle S_z\rangle(t)$ before looking at the traces.
Start along $+z$ with $\vec B\parallel\hat z$: why is nothing happening? Which states are eigenstates of $H$?
Tilt $\vec B$ by 90° (towards $x$): predict which components oscillate for a spin starting along $z$.
Switch the field off: what does the time evolution of $\langle\vec S\rangle$ look like, and which energies would the two levels have?

source.where: spin-1/2 in a magnetic field, Larmor precession (angular-momentum-spin room sources)

enc.title: Avoided crossing: second-order theory and its breakdown
enc.intro: Two levels coupled by $V$: the lower exact level against second-order perturbation theory $\varepsilon_1-V^2/\Delta$. Use it to see where the condition $|V|\ll|E_n-E_m|$ of the FS19/HS18 Q4 derivation holds.
tasks: Predict the exact gap at $\Delta=0$ for $V=0.5$ (it is $2V$), then read it off the plot.
Increase $V$ with the second-order curve on: at which $\Delta$ does it start to deviate by more than the line width? Compare with $|\Delta|\approx2V$.
At $\Delta=0$ the levels are degenerate: degenerate PT gives $\pm V$ (the Stark effect $n=2$ is exactly this $2\times2$ problem with $V=3|e|Ea_0$). Check that the exact curve agrees.
Which side is pushed down: the level with a neighbour above or below? (the one with a neighbour above, as the ground state in FS19 Q4)
